COMMENT: What each program can be told, over what it does on its own. Leave a value out and the program keeps its built in one; a key no program knows is an error rather than a silent no-op, so a misspelt name is noticed at startup.

The end of a name says what the number costs to run. A _PAUSE is time the program really spends, every time, whether or not anything was going to happen - that is where a program gets faster. An _INTERVAL is the gap between two looks at the same thing, spent over and over, but only while that wait lasts. A _TIMEOUT is an upper bound and is only ever paid when something has gone wrong, so raising one costs nothing until it does. A _RETRIES is a number of attempts.

How long a click waits for the game to show it was taken, and how many times it is repeated, are the same for every program and live in eve_config.json as CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT and ACTION_RETRIES_DEFAULT.

PROGRAMS.NAME: undock
PROGRAMS.COMMENT: UNDOCK_BUTTON_TIMEOUT covers finding the undock button, or settling that the ship was never docked. UNDOCK_CLICK_PAUSE is the moment given to the click itself before anything is looked for. IN_SPACE_TIMEOUT then runs until the ship core says the ship is out, which takes as long as the undock animation does.

PROGRAMS.NAME: autopilot
PROGRAMS.COMMENT: DESTINATION_TIMEOUT waits for a gate or station icon in the route panel. WARP_TIMEOUT covers the whole warp, from the command being taken until the warp message has both appeared and gone away again. RECHECK_INTERVAL is the gap between two looks at the same thing - an empty route panel, or a warp still going on. GATE_JUMP_PAUSE and DOCKING_PAUSE let the session change or the docking animation finish, and DOCKING_TIMEOUT waits for the undock button that proves the ship is inside.
